# F8-02: MTU 1280 on the rendered exit path — 2026-10-31

TEST ONLY kernel lab measurement for AT09 / EXIT02 / APP01 / NFR01 (§19),
IPv6 mode (§8.3), isolation (§8.2) and shaping (§11.4). Production code is
unchanged. Measurement source: `ae318a4`; final traffic window
**10:03:56–10:04:47 UTC** on amd64. Arm64 is cross-built, not hardware-tested.

**IPv4: complete transfer and PMTU error traversal observed at MTU 1280.**
The reconnect transfer returned 64,064/64,064 bytes in 2.899 ms; steady state
returned 64,064/64,064 in 4.392 ms. Neither reproduces the partial native transfer.

**IPv6: MTU 1280 is configured on the exit link, but end-to-end member
forwarding is unavailable.** The rendered policy deliberately drops IPv6 in
both directions. TCP SYNs and injected forwarded packet-too-big errors reach
the node and increment `ctv6`; no member class dequeue follows. Locally
generated packet-too-big errors do return to the member via the host class.
No different MTU or IPv6 allow rule was substituted to obtain a success.

The [members request](../e2e/at/members/requests.md#f8-02--mtu-1280-bulk-transfer-incomplete),
[NATIVE.md](../e2e/at/members/NATIVE.md) and
[AT09.json](../e2e/at/members/AT09.json) distinguish **underlay family** from
IPv6 overlay forwarding. Their failed dual-underlay/1280 row returned
11,011/64,064 bytes in 12,011 ms, with direct IPv4 selected before and after,
and counter deltas 66,296 upload / 45,963 download. That remains failed. This
lab runs kernel WireGuard over a fixed IPv4 underlay; it does not run native
NetBird down/up, ICE, relay selection, or the members' application fixture.
Consequently it cannot assign the original native partial-transfer cause to
NetBird or clear that row.

## Method and evidence

The normal lab `functionalModel` is installed through verified `enforce.Apply`
at generation 802. It retains `ipv6_mode=block`, the original `inet fvpn`
chains, HTB and fq_codel. The path is member `fv-a1/fv-wg0` → routing namespace
→ node `fv-fh` → node `fv-ih` → controlled origin `fv-inet/fv-ii`. The inner
WireGuard interface stays at 1420. Both ends of the exit veth (`fv-ih` and
`fv-ii`) are set to **1280**, which applies to both IP families; read-back is
in `links-1280.json`. The 1500 rows below are explicitly preceding controls,
not replacements for either family's 1280 row.

`mtu_measure.py` starts a dual-stack TCP echo server at the controlled origin,
then records the following sequence, without transfer retries:

1. Recreate the member's kernel WireGuard interface, restore its fixture
   addresses/routes, and immediately start a new TCP connection and 64,064-byte
   transfer. No warm-up probe or sleep intervenes. Do this in row order
   IPv4/1500, IPv6/1500, both inner families/1500, both inner families/1280.
   Each inner-family attempt recreates the interface. This models reconnect
   timing only; it does not emulate native dual-underlay selection.
2. Retain the tunnel, then perform steady-state transfers for both families at
   1280. Each client has a 12 s total deadline and checks all returned bytes.
3. Send oversized DF IPv4 and IPv6 echo probes (1360-byte payload), followed
   by 1200-byte probes. Record the genuine kernel-generated MTU errors.
4. Establish a controlled IPv4 UDP tuple and observe its actual SNAT address
   and port. Inject ICMP type 3/code 4 errors quoting that tuple in **both
   directions**, advertising 1280. These are explicit error-traversal probes,
   not claims that a downstream router discovered another bottleneck.
   Inject ICMPv6 type 2 errors in both directions as block-policy controls;
   IPv6 has no established member flow to quote.

Before measurement the fixture installs two permanent IPv6 neighbors on the
member-side transit veth. Normal neighbor solicitation on `fv-fh` hits the
rendered input rule `iifname "fv-fh" counter name "ctin" drop`. Earlier capture
shows this directly. `transit-before.json` proves the addresses already exist;
`transit-static-neighbors.json` records the fixture assistance. This enables
packets to reach the forward hook without changing input or forward policy.
It is not a production IPv6 enablement or a NetBird repair.

Three independent `any` tcpdump captures (member, node, origin) retain only
header text, including ICMP error/quoted IP headers and TCP MSS options.
There is no payload dump. All final captures have **zero kernel drops** and
exact header-count equality: **576 member, 1117 node, 541 origin**. Multicast
neighbor-discovery headers count too. Each phase records realtime start/end,
command results, nft counters and raw tc class/qdisc/filter read-back.

All final inputs, [analysis](G2-followup18-evidence/mtu/TestAT09_F802_MTU1280Measurement/analysis.txt)
and [capture checks](G2-followup18-evidence/mtu/TestAT09_F802_MTU1280Measurement/capture-checks.json)
are under `G2-followup18-evidence/mtu/TestAT09_F802_MTU1280Measurement/`.
The original three unsuccessful collector attempts remain in `mtu-attempt1`,
`mtu-attempt2`, `mtu-attempt3`: the first two stopped before traffic because
the collector expected JSON from tc; raw text read-back removes that
assumption. The third completed traffic but failed header-count equality
because the first parser omitted 53 multicast rows. It also exposed the
neighbor-discovery limitation. Those files retain their original failures;
only the final independent run is the completed measurement.

## Transfer and MSS results

| Phase | Inner family | Exit MTU | Bytes returned | Elapsed (ms) | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Reconnect, first row | IPv4 | 1500 | 64064 | 2.807 | complete |
| Reconnect, second row | IPv6 | 1500 | 0 | 12011.962 | SYNs dropped by IPv6 policy |
| Reconnect, both-family row | IPv4 | 1500 | 64064 | 2.463 | complete |
| Reconnect, both-family row | IPv6 | 1500 | 0 | 12003.260 | SYNs dropped by IPv6 policy |
| Reconnect, both-family row | IPv4 | **1280** | **64064** | **2.899** | complete |
| Reconnect, both-family row | IPv6 | **1280** | **0** | **12012.262** | SYNs dropped by IPv6 policy |
| Steady state | IPv4 | **1280** | **64064** | **4.392** | complete |
| Steady state | IPv6 | **1280** | **0** | **12012.298** | SYNs dropped by IPv6 policy |

There is **no TCP MSS clamp in the rendered exit rules or tc filters**.
The captured IPv4 SYN advertises **1380** at member egress, node ingress,
node exit and origin ingress, unchanged across the node. At MTU 1280 the
origin advertises **1240** in its SYN-ACK, also unchanged at every return hop.
The client reports `TCP_MAXSEG=1228` with timestamp options negotiated. At
1500 the origin advertises 1460 and the client reports 1368. The endpoint's
MSS advertisement is not an exit clamp.

IPv6 SYNs advertise **1360** at member egress and node ingress. There is no
exit SYN or SYN-ACK, so an on-wire IPv6 exit/negotiated MSS value is **not
available**. Neither rendered nft rules nor tc contain an MSS rewrite; there
is no basis to report an invented IPv6 clamp value of 1220. Native NetBird's
MSS behavior is outside this kernel fixture.

## PMTU, rules and tc in both directions

| Probe at MTU 1280 | Independent packet observations | nft/counter evidence | tc evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| IPv4 oversized DF request, 1388 IP bytes | Node generates fragmentation-needed/1280; node `fv-fh Out` and member `fv-wg0 In` | No forwarding admission increment for the rejected oversized packet; local output chain permits reply | `fv-fh` host class `1:fffe`: +1 packet, 590 bytes, zero drops |
| IPv4 1228-byte IP request | Origin reached and echo returned | Upload and download each +1 packet / 1228 IP bytes | Member class `1:2f`: +1 / 1242 bytes each direction, zero drops |
| Quoted IPv4 error toward member | Origin Out → node `fv-ih In` → `fv-fh Out` → member In | Reverse SNAT restores member/quoted tuple; download +1 / 64 IP bytes | `fv-fh` member class `1:2f`: +1 / 78 bytes, zero drops |
| Quoted IPv4 error toward origin | Member Out → node `fv-fh In` → `fv-ih Out` → origin In | SNAT rewrites outer/quoted tuple; upload +1 / 64 IP bytes | `fv-ih` member class `1:2f`: +1 / 78 bytes, zero drops |
| IPv6 oversized request, 1408 IP bytes | Node generates packet-too-big/1280; node `fv-fh Out` and member In | Local output, no `ctv6`/admission increment | `fv-fh` host class: +1 / 1294 bytes, zero drops |
| IPv6 1248-byte IP request | Member Out → node `fv-fh In`; no origin packet | `ctv6` +1 / 1248 bytes | No class dequeue increment |
| Quoted IPv6 error toward member | Origin Out → node `fv-ih In`; no node/member egress | `ctv6` +1 / 104 bytes | No member-class dequeue; unrelated neighbor advertisement uses uplink host class |
| Quoted IPv6 error toward origin | Member Out → node `fv-fh In`; no node/origin egress | `ctv6` +1 / 104 bytes | No class dequeue increment |

The 14-byte difference between nft IP-byte counts and tc byte counts is
retained explicitly; these are different layers, not loss. A locally generated
MTU error uses the node's output/host class and does **not** prove that a
forwarded error can pass the forward chain. The quoted probes provide that
separate evidence. The final IPv6 small-packet and both error negatives reach
the node, avoiding an inference from a connection timeout alone.

Exact relevant rendered rules (`initial.json` / `final.json`, unchanged):

```nft
iifname "fv-fh" oifname "fv-ih" meta nfproto ipv6 counter name "ctv6" drop
iifname "fv-ih" oifname "fv-fh" meta nfproto ipv6 counter name "ctv6" drop
iifname "fv-ih" oifname "fv-fh" ip daddr != @allowed_v4 counter name "ctunkd" drop
iifname "fv-ih" oifname "fv-fh" ct state != { established, related } counter name "ctnodn" drop
```

The verified IPv4 per-device accepts after these guards set priority `0x0001002f`;
the returned error therefore uses the same member leaf as ordinary traffic.
The upload per-device accept likewise assigns that leaf. There is no separate
missing IPv4 ICMP allow rule demonstrated here: related errors traverse it.
No MSS-setting rule exists. The IPv6 drops precede the IPv4 admission paths;
no IPv6 PMTU-forwarding exception is implemented.

### Requests to orchestrator

1. **Owner: `node/enforce`, IPv6 support boundary.** The observed IPv6 forward
   rejection is exactly the two `meta nfproto ipv6 ... ctv6 drop` rules in
   `node/enforce/render_nft.go`; `validate.go` accepts only `IPv6Block`.
   Keep IPv6 end-to-end PMTU/transfer acceptance unavailable under the current
   §8.3 mode. If IPv6 overlay forwarding is required, assign a separate design
   and implementation task for validation, admission, verification, metering,
   ND and ICMPv6 handling. Do not remove these rules merely to pass this lab.
   The fixture's static-neighbor assistance is recorded above.
2. **Owner: w3-devstack-e2e / native fixture investigation for the original
   F8-02 row.** Carry the unchanged 11,011-byte failure forward. This lab has
   no IPv4 nft/tc failure or required MSS clamp to hand off as its cause; it
   cannot distinguish native NetBird reconnect behavior from the original
   fixture's read/echo behavior. Retain native per-hop SYN/MSS, ICMP errors,
   interface MTUs and application read counts on that same reconnect row
   before assigning a product fix. No out-of-scope file change is established
   by this measurement, and no native-stack acceptance is promoted.

## Reproduce

Check the shared-host slot before starting; wait while two other suites run.
This launcher uses Python teardown, disk temp directories and only lane-owned
Docker objects. Remove the task-tagged image after the final run.

```sh
pgrep -af 'gates.sh|mk/at-'
FVPN_LAB_PREFIX=fvpn-w1-netlab-f18 FVPN_NETLAB_MTU=1 \
FVPN_NETLAB_EVIDENCE_DIR=.agent/f18-mtu-reproduction \
python3 tests/netlab/scripts/disktmp.py \
  python3 tests/netlab/scripts/scenario_run.py '^TestAT09_F802_MTU1280Measurement$'
python3 -B tests/netlab/scripts/mtu_analysis.py \
  docs/poc/G2-followup18-evidence/mtu/TestAT09_F802_MTU1280Measurement \
  --output .agent/tmp/f802-analysis.json
```

The measurement test passes when collection and checked capture retention
complete; its pass is **not** an IPv6 transfer or native AT09 acceptance pass.
The three task verdicts are AT10 PASS under D-120, IPv4 MTU-1280 measured
complete, and IPv6 MTU-1280 end-to-end service unavailable under rendered policy.
